comments.body: I hope you don't take it as me bothering you, but maybe it would be better for the end user to expose the keys of this PR in `lspconfig` instead of `rustaceanvim`'s `on_attach` function, so it's easier for them to change them if they want to? Otherwise the user would have to mess with the `config` function to do that?

I'm not very familiar with how lazy works, but rustaceanvim is opinionated in the sense that it doesn't want `lspconfig` to handle anything related to `rust_analyzer`. They explicitly state to put them inside the `on_attach` function, like @appelgriebsch did.

Would disabling everything but the keys in the `lspconfig` work?

Could you add the `dap` and `tools` sections from 

https://github.com/LazyVim/LazyVim/discussions/1976#discussioncomment-7912177

Could you add: `vim.lsp.inlay_hint.enable(bufnr, true)` to have inlay hints enable by default, like with `rust-analyzer`. 

This will only work with neovim's builtin inlay hints, which I think are only in nightly. That's why @trevarj was saying in the discussion "it is probably not worth migrating until nvim 0.10".
I tried it and didn't work, that's why the final commit put them in the `on_attach` function instead.

`dap` is automatically configured in rustacean.nvim when installed via mason (similar to what we had before) -> https://github.com/mrcjkb/rustaceanvim/blob/master/lua/rustaceanvim/config/internal.lua#L207

shouldn't that be part of core LazyVim LspAttach functionality when it's running with neovim >= 0.10.x? see here: https://github.com/LazyVim/LazyVim/blob/879e29504d43e9f178d967ecc34d482f902e5a91/lua/lazyvim/plugins/lsp/init.lua#L119-L121
Are they being enabled by default for you? I tried late last night, and they weren't for me. Maybe I had other issues, I'll try again.
Awesome. When I tried it, it wasn't by default 👍
hmmm might be related to this: https://github.com/appelgriebsch/Nv/blob/main/lua/plugins/lang.lua#L6

When I call `:lua print(vim.fn.has('nvim-0.10'))` it prints `1`

```
λ ➜ nvim --version
NVIM v0.10.0-dev-1890+g1cf51a07a
Build type: RelWithDebInfo
LuaJIT 2.1.1702233742
Run "nvim -V1 -v" for more info
```
Tried it and works great 🔥
They only enable for me when I start typing in insert mode and then <esc>ing and saving

For neovim < 0.10, there's [a separate plugin](https://github.com/lvimuser/lsp-inlayhints.nvim) that enables inlay hints.
There's also [one by simrat39](https://github.com/simrat39/inlay-hints.nvim), the rust-tools author, which is based on the implementation in rust-tools.

The existence of those two plugins + the built-in support after nvim 0.10 was the reason I decided to drop inlay hints from rustaceanvim.

I don't remember how good the performance was in rust-tools, but compared to the nvim 0.10 implementation, it [appears to be quite slow with both plugins](https://github.com/mrcjkb/rustaceanvim/discussions/46#discussioncomment-7697717).

I suppose you could in theory add one of the plugins as a plugin spec with `optional = vim.fn.has('nvim-0.10')`.

suggestion: Change this key to `default_settings`, as this will allow users
to override it with a project-local rust-analyzer.json.

FYI I'm thinking about adding the clippy lints by default, if rustaceanvim detects a clippy installation.
+1 for clippy, it's so useful

Just pushed a release with clippy auto-detection :smile: 
It can be disabled with the `tools.enable_clippy` option or by explicitly setting the `checkOnSave` config to something else.
updated

This may want to be moved to the `dependencies` section of `mrcjkb/rustaceanvim`. 

Currently rustaceanvim will only use neotest as it's `test_executor` if the `rustaceanvim.neotest` module was loaded prior to rustaceanvim being configured. (https://github.com/mrcjkb/rustaceanvim/blob/4.7.0/lua/rustaceanvim/config/internal.lua#L42-L48)
rustaceanvim loads its configuration lazily (when opening a rust file). So it should still pick up the neotest config as long as neotest isn't lazy loaded by lazy.nvim.
I'm curious about why these 3 macros were singled out?
